entries.msgstr: Battle Pass is a game event where players complete Progression Stages, earn Points, and receive valuable rewards. As a reward for completing certain Stages, players receive Battle Pass Tokens, a special currency that can be used to purchase unique vehicles and other useful items in the corresponding section of the in-game Store.
About Battle Pass
Every day, you can complete several missions and monitor their progress. For completing them, you will be rewarded with Progression Points and credits.
Every day, you can complete several missions and monitor their progress. For completing them, you will be rewarded with Progression Points, Steel Seals, and credits.
Missions
Solo Battle
Platoon Battle

%(place)s places
The mode will be available from %(startDate)s through %(endDate)s

Get your well-deserved rewards in battles!
Hunting season starts now!
Each vehicle has two common and two unique Combat Abilities, along with the Respawn mechanic.

In the Garage, you will find eight special vehicles of three types. They differ in their tactical uses and unique features. Their configuration cannot be modified in the Garage, but all vehicles have their own set of modules that can be upgraded in battle.
Hunters
Shamrock has turned all yellow Spoils of War green, but they still contain everything you need: XP, hit point recovery, shells, charges for Abilities, and, most importantly, Lucky Seals.
Paint It Green!

To earn Seals, collect Spoils of War in battle, complete Progression Stages, and take the top positions in this battle royale. When playing in a Platoon, all earned Lucky Seals are distributed evenly between Platoon members. You can also earn two times more Seals once a day for the first battle fought in each event vehicle. To activate the bonus, you need to perform well in battle.
Lucky Seals
Fight in Steel Hunter to earn Lucky Seals that can be exchanged for special rewards in the Shamrock Shop.
Special Rewards
Arzagir 4.04
Dreamland
Firnulfir

The hunt will take place on three maps: {{@ colorLegacy 'ede6d9e5'}}Arzagir 4.04, Dreamland, and Firnulfir{{/}}. These maps are larger than those in Random Battles. The first map depicts an open desert area with sand pits and dry creeks. The second is a dense urban area where you can easily hide from the enemy. And the third represents a snowy tundra in Scandinavia, with its characteristic rolling terrain, small villages, and frozen ponds.
Three Maps
Destroy Marauders to get some good loot.
{{@ colorLegacy 'eeede9'}}Hare{{/}} — cowardly but fast
{{@ colorLegacy 'eeede9'}}Wolf{{/}} — an aggressive fighter that attacks and pursues its prey
{{@ colorLegacy 'eeede9'}}Bear{{/}} — a formidable rival that protects its territory fiercely
A group of AI-driven vehicles that scavenge the remains of vehicles scattered across the maps after Steel Hunter tournaments. They pose no threat in battle. The following types have been detected:
Marauders
Battle royale in vehicles that can be upgraded in battle.
Steel Hunter
Battle royale in vehicles that can be upgraded in battle.
Steel Hunter

Earn two times more Seals once a day for the first battle fought in each special vehicle. To activate the bonus, be among the top 10 players in a solo battle or among top 7 players when fighting in a Platoon.
Twofold Lucky Seals
All event vehicles are available for free. Steel Seals can be exchanged for customization elements.
Economy

A special currency that can be exchanged for valuable items in the Shamrock Shop. Collect Spoils of War in battle, complete Progression Stages, and win battle royale battles to earn as many Lucky Seals as possible. When playing in a Platoon, all Seals you earn are distributed between Platoon members.
Lucky Seals
Aim for high results in the battles and complete missions to advance through the Progression.
Progression
Complete daily missions and take the top positions in battles to complete Progression Stages and earn various rewards, including Lucky Seals.
Progression
The Respawn mechanic allows you to get back to battle after your vehicle is destroyed. The vehicle's upgrade level is not lost in this case.
Respawn
General Information

A special Battle Pass resource that can be earned across different modes, including Steel Hunter. The number of Points earned depends on your position in the battle results. Steel Hunter vehicles do not have Point Limits.
Battle Pass Points
The top hunter in a battle receives bonus Lucky Seals. You will also receive additional Progression Points after each battle depending on your position in the battle results.
Bonus for Position in Battle Results
After each battle, you will receive a number of Progression Points corresponding to your position in the battle results.
Point Distribution

Participate in Shamrock Showdown and receive valuable rewards! To advance through the Progression, you will need special Points that can be earned by completing the event's daily missions and fighting in Steel Hunter battles.
After completing the Main Progression, you can continue fighting battles and earning Lucky Seals. Exchange them for special rewards in the Shamrock Shop.
Lucky Seals

Complete the Hunter's Path and receive valuable rewards! To advance through the Progression, you will need special Points that can be earned by completing the event's daily missions and fighting in Steel Hunter battles.
After completing the Main Progression, you can continue completing missions and earn Steel Seals that you can exchange for customization elements in the in-game Store.
Progression
Steel Seals

Radio Detection allows you to pinpoint enemy vehicles and drops on the minimap. The system is activated manually by pressing the X key. It can be reactivated after some time. In addition, you can increase the radius of Radio Detection or reduce its cooldown by researching the corresponding technologies in battle.

Polish engineers know that emphasizing one of a vehicle's strong suits automatically results in the deterioration of another characteristic. That's why they gave enough consideration to the vehicle's armament and combat abilities to prevent the enemy from seeking out its weak spots. As time would tell, that proved to be the right decision.
Radio Detection
Once destroyed, your vehicle respawns automatically. This mechanic works within the first {{@ colorLegacy 'eeede9'}}{{soloRespawnPeriod}} min{{/}} of a battle.
When Playing Solo

To respawn an ally, stay out of combat during {{@ colorLegacy 'eeede9'}}{{platoonTimeToResurrect}} s{{/}}. This mechanic works within the first {{@ colorLegacy 'eeede9'}}{{platoonRespawnPeriod}} min{{/}} of a battle. Respawn charges are shared between Platoon members.
When Playing in a Platoon
This mechanic allows you to get back to battle after your vehicle is destroyed. The vehicle's upgrade level is not lost in this case.
Respawn
The new visibility system is based on cone view range. If enemies, Spoils of War, or Airdrop are not located within the Vision Cone, you will not see them.

If an enemy vehicle gets too close to you, it will be spotted automatically. Take note that, in battle, you can receive damage without seeing your attacker. Your vehicle's Vision Cone is "tied" to your turret, so be sure to rotate it to look around and spot your target.
Vision Cone
Lucky Seals that you earn can be exchanged for special Steel Hunter rewards in a special section of the Store.
You can exchange Steel Seals for Steel Hunter styles and decals in the corresponding section of the in-game Store.
{{@ colorLegacy 'ecca9d'}}With WoT Premium Account, you earn more Steel Seals in battle.{{/}}
Store

Get your well-deserved rewards in battles.
Let the hunting season begin!
SHAMROCK SHOWDOWN
After each battle, you will receive a number of Battle Pass Points corresponding to your position in the battle results.
Point Distribution
STEEL HUNTER

Restores hit points, repairs modules, and contains everything you need for battle: a Recovery charge, shells, and XP for upgrading your vehicle, as well as, with a certain probability, a charge for Repair Kit or one of the unique Combat Abilities.
Consumables

Repairs modules, restores hit points, and contains a charge for Recovery, ammo, and experience for improving the vehicle. This loot allows you to level up your vehicle faster, as well as promptly prepare for battle.
Consumables

If you get your hands on an Airdrop, you will get a Respawn charge—and a huge advantage over your opponents. This is the most valuable drop, and it restores hit points and repairs your vehicle's modules. It also contains XP, ammo, and charges for all four Abilities. Picking up an Airdrop takes more time. The Airdrop landing zone can also be seen by all hunters on their minimaps, so getting hold of one can be challenging.
Airdrop

Contains XP, although in smaller quantities than the Consumables loot type, and ammo. It may also contain a charge for Repair Kit or one of the unique Combat Abilities. Finding this loot can give you a chance to turn the tide of battle.
Supplies

To upgrade your vehicle, look out for special locations with loot containing XP for vehicle upgrades, as well as ammunition and charges for Combat Abilities. The number of items depends on the loot type.
Loot

After destroying an enemy, you can pick up half of their Ability charges, restore hit points, and repair your vehicle's damaged modules, as well as receive XP and ammo. You also have a chance to get an extra charge for one of the four Abilities. Destroyed vehicles that contain Spoils of War are marked with red smoke on the map. Picking up this drop type takes less time.
Spoils of War
Cowering in the corner is not an option. This mode is for those who favor a fair fight. The map shrinks over time, decreasing the playable area and forcing Hunters to meet face to face.
This happens at random, and how often depends on the number of vehicles in battle. Take heed and try to leave unsafe areas in advance.
Shrinking Game Zone
In a destruction zone, your vehicle will gradually lose hit points until completely destroyed. You will have very little time to leave the destruction area.
Red: Destruction Zone
Your vehicle takes no damage in a danger zone, but a square of this color can close at any time. Plan your retreat accordingly.
Yellow: Danger Zone
